svg.title: The Periodontium: Four Components in One Section
svg.desc: A schematic facial tooth section shows gingiva, periodontal ligament, cementum, and alveolar bone together. Magnified sections show the junctional epithelium basal laminae, bone and fiber attachment, and the anatomy that requires adjacent teeth or multiple roots.
svg.text: L1b · Periodontal Health / Schematic facial section with magnified relationships
Protective soft tissue around the tooth
Two attachment interfaces: tooth-facing and connective-tissue-facing. L1b pp. 23–27.
LD Lamina densa · LL Lamina lucida · CT Connective tissue
Magenta brackets show hemidesmosomes at the JE–lamina lucida interface.
The principal fiber continues through the PDL and embeds into mineralized tissue at both ends.
Socket wall: lamina dura on radiographs; cribriform perforations carry vessels and nerves. L1b pp. 39, 65, 69.
C · Between teeth, around a tooth, and between roots
These three relationships need a different section plane or more than one root. L1b pp. 10–11, 34–35, 41–42, 47.
Companion schematics use the same colors as the main section.
Blood supply: supraperiosteal, PDL, and interdental vessels.
Crevicular fluid enters the sulcus. L1b pp. 28–30, 36.
Acellular: mainly cervical · Cellular: common apically
Cementocytes lie in lacunae. L1b pp. 52–58.
Periosteum covers the bone. L1b pp. 70, 73.
GM → sulcus → JE at its base
CEJ separates crown and root coverings
Sharpey’s fibers embed at both ends
